planting.note: Root tip cuttings in moist potting mix in spring, since Icterina does not come true from seed. Plant in well-drained, lean, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun after last frost.

directions: Root tip cuttings in moist potting mix in spring or summer and plant in well-drained, lean, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Icterina is a variegated culinary sage with soft gray-green leaves broadly edged in gold, giving a brighter, more luminous look to an herb garden or mixed border than plain green sage while carrying the same savory, slightly peppery flavor used in stuffings, poultry dishes, and herb butters. It stays a bit more compact than green garden sage, making it useful for edging or container plantings. Cut back hard in early spring to remove winter-worn growth and encourage fresh, well-colored new leaves.

planting.note: Amazel is a sterile hybrid basil bred for strong resistance to downy mildew, a disease that devastates sweet basil in humid climates; because it does not flower or set seed, all energy goes into vigorous, extended leaf production.

directions: Transplant into warm, rich, well-drained soil in full sun only after all frost danger passes. Amazel was bred specifically to resist downy mildew, a fungal disease that can wipe out a planting of traditional Genovese basil in a single humid season, and because the plant is sterile it never flowers or goes to seed, channeling all of its energy into continuous, vigorous leaf growth all season long. The flavor is classic sweet basil, well suited to pesto and general cooking, and the plant's disease resistance and non-flowering habit make it especially valuable for humid Gulf South gardens where downy mildew is a persistent problem. Because it is propagated from cuttings rather than seed, plants are typically purchased as starts.
sources: Cornell Cooperative Extension — Basil Downy Mildew

planting.note: Prospera is a downy-mildew-resistant series bred to keep the classic Genovese basil flavor and growth habit while resisting the fungal disease that devastates sweet basil in humid climates.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into warm, rich, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger passes. Bred through conventional breeding to carry strong resistance to downy mildew, Prospera keeps the familiar large-leaved, classic sweet flavor and growth habit of Genovese basil while standing up far better to the humid conditions that favor mildew outbreaks in traditional pesto basil. Pinch growing tips to encourage bushy growth and harvest whole stems above a leaf node, removing flower buds promptly to keep the leaves tender. Its disease resistance makes it a strong choice for humid Gulf South gardens where standard Genovese basil often declines by midsummer.
sources: Cornell Cooperative Extension — Basil Downy Mildew

planting.note: Windowbox is a dwarf, mounding basil bred specifically for small containers and windowsill growing, staying compact without becoming leggy.

directions: Start seed indoors or direct sow after the last frost, and grow in a container or small bed in full sun. This compact, naturally mounding basil was selected specifically for small spaces, staying dense and tidy in a windowsill pot or patio container rather than stretching tall and leggy like standard Genovese basil. The small, aromatic leaves have classic sweet basil flavor and are well suited to snipping a few at a time for garnish and light cooking use. Regular light pinching keeps the plant full and encourages continuous new growth through the season.

common_name: Everleaf Thai Basil (Non-Flowering Extended-Harvest Thai Basil)

planting.note: Everleaf Thai is a non-flowering hybrid selected to hold classic anise-clove Thai basil flavor and columnar growth without bolting to seed, extending the usable harvest window compared to standard Thai basil.

directions: Start seed indoors or transplant into warm, rich, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger passes. Part of the Everleaf breeding series that also produced Everleaf Emerald Towers, this Thai-type basil carries the classic anise-clove flavor and purple-tinged stems and flower bracts of traditional Thai basil, but its non-flowering habit means the plant keeps producing fresh, flavorful leaves for weeks longer than seed-setting types before quality declines. The upright, columnar growth habit also makes it a good choice for narrow spaces and containers. Harvest by cutting whole stem tips, which encourages continued branching and leaf production through the season.
sources: Proven Harvest / Pan American Seed reference
